turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, have a seat. I see you've got someone with you. What's been happening with the skin?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, Doctor, it's this rash. It started yesterday morning, proper itchy, on my arms first, and then it crept onto my tummy and my chest. I've been scratching like mad, even at the till at the Spar in Durbanville, which is embarrassing when there's a queue.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Itchy rash since yesterday morning, arms then tummy and chest. Have you felt feverish, or had a temperature with it?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no temperature. I haven't felt feverish at all. I've been fine in myself, it's just the itch driving me mad.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling of the lips or the tongue, or trouble getting your breath?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing like that. Breathing is normal, and my lips are normal. I checked in the car mirror on the way over.
[SEG0007] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She was scratching the whole way from Durbanville, Doctor, I can vouch for that. I'm her sister, by the way.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thanks. What do you think set it off? Anything new in the last few days?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the whole problem, I honestly don't know. It could be something I ate, or this new cream I started putting on, or the antibiotic. I keep going round in circles and I can't say which one it is.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let's take them one by one. What did you eat that you're wondering about?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Friday night we had prawns at my brother's braai in Bellville. I had a decent portion with garlic butter, and I've eaten prawns plenty of times before, so I don't know why they'd suddenly turn on me. The rash only came yesterday, though, which feels a bit late if it was the prawns.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Prawns on Friday, rash from yesterday morning. Tell me about the cream.

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): It's Epimax cream, from the chemist. I started it three days ago for the dry skin on my shins, twice a day, morning and after my shower. It's not even on my arms, which is where the rash is worst, so it doesn't quite make sense, but it's new so I thought I should say.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Epimax twice a day for three days, on the shins. And the antibiotic, what's the name and the dose?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Amoxicillin, five hundred milligrams, by mouth, three times a day. The GP at the day hospital started it four days ago for a sinus infection. I've taken every dose, breakfast, lunch and supper, I haven't missed one.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Amoxicillin five hundred milligrams three times a day by mouth for four days, for the sinus infection, and you're still taking it. Any vomiting, or pain in the joints?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting, and my joints are fine. I made sure to eat with the tablets so they wouldn't upset my stomach.

[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Can I just say something? This is the same thing that happened with penicillin when she was small. She came out in hives all over, and our mother still talks about it.

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, no, that's not right. That was our cousin Lerato, not me. I've never had a penicillin allergy, and I took penicillin for tonsillitis in high school and I was completely fine.

[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): So you don't recall any penicillin reaction yourself, but your sister remembers hives when you were small. I'll note that the two of you don't agree, and I won't mark you down as penicillin-allergic just on that.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, before we carry on, the traffic on the N1 was completely hectic this morning. We sat at that robot by the Century City turnoff for ages.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, and then she wanted to talk about the Proteas the whole time we were stuck. Did you see the match last night, Doctor?
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): I caught the last few overs. Bavuma's innings was lovely, hey, proper batting.

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Lovely is the word. My nephew was jumping on the couch shouting at the TV, and my sister had to hide the remote from him. We nearly missed this appointment because of that robot, never mind the cricket.
[SEG0025] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Next time we're leaving earlier, cricket or no cricket. The weather was nice at least, not too hot sitting in the car.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Glad you got here. Let me have a proper look at the rash.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): It's a red, bumpy rash on both forearms and across the tummy. There are no blisters, and your lips aren't swollen.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pulse is 82, temperature is 36.8, and the blood pressure is 128 over 76.

[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, while you're writing that down, I need to correct myself. Last night and again this morning I did feel hot and shivery, like a fever coming on. I even opened the bedroom window, and my sister said I felt warm, so I was wrong when I said I hadn't felt feverish.

[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that's worth knowing. You've felt hot and shivery since last night, even though the thermometer here is normal. Any cough or sore throat still, with that sinus infection?

[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough and no sore throat. The sinus pain is much better, almost gone, it was sitting right over my cheeks last week. The itch is the main thing now, and it's worse at night, I was awake till past one scratching.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me summarise it back. Itchy rash since yesterday morning on the arms, tummy and chest, worse at night, you've felt hot and shivery since last night, you're on amoxicillin five hundred milligrams three times a day by mouth for a sinus infection, Epimax on the shins twice a day for three days, and prawns on Friday. You and your sister disagree about childhood penicillin hives, and there's been no lip swelling, no breathing trouble and no vomiting. Does that match?

[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, that's fair. I've also had hay fever every spring since I was a teenager, itchy eyes and sneezing, but that's not playing up now. I'm not a smoker, I've never smoked, and I live with my sister in Durbanville.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She hardly drinks either, maybe one glass of wine at a braai, and that's it.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Noted. I'm not going to pin this on one cause. It may be a reaction to the amoxicillin, or to the Epimax, or to the prawns, and I can't separate them today, so I wouldn't call it a definite allergy.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So what do we actually do, because the itch is really getting to me and I can't concentrate at the till. If I stop the antibiotic I'm worried the sinus thing comes roaring back, it was bad last week. I don't want to mess this up by guessing.

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'd like you to stop the amoxicillin and stop the Epimax for now, and stay off prawns until we know more. For the itch I'll prescribe cetirizine, ten milligrams by mouth, once at night.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Cetirizine at night, ja, I can manage that. Do I start it tonight, and do I just leave the rest of the amoxicillin box in the cupboard?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Start the cetirizine tonight, and don't take any more of the amoxicillin. If the rash is not better in two weeks, come back and see me.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it hasn't settled by then, we might also arrange a patch test, to look at the cream and other things touching the skin. I won't book that today.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): A patch test, okay. Will that tell you about the prawns as well, or only about creams and stuff on the skin? I just want to understand what I'm agreeing to.

[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Patch testing is for things that touch the skin, not for food and not for the antibiotic. Those we judge from the story and from how you do once they're stopped. If your lip or tongue swells, or you can't breathe, go to casualty straight away, don't wait for the two weeks.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll keep an eye on her at home. She does minimise things, you saw that with the fever story.

[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't minimise, I just like to get it accurate before I say it. I'll stop the tablets and the cream, take the cetirizine tonight, and I'll come back if the rash is not better in two weeks.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. The script will be waiting at reception. Go carefully on that N1.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Thanks, Doctor. Cheerio.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.

omissions.text: Sinus pain is much better/almost gone, rather than simply current/present.
Amoxicillin was specifically started by the GP at the day hospital four days ago, and the patient had taken every dose without missing any.
Epimax cream was obtained from the chemist and applied to the shins morning and after shower; the rash is worst on the arms where the cream was not applied.

No temperature/fever was initially denied, but this was later corrected: the patient felt hot and shivery last night and this morning, and her sister said she felt warm, despite a normal measured temperature in clinic. The recorded facts do not capture the corrected contradiction about feverishness.
Rash spread pattern was stated: started on the arms first, then spread to the tummy and chest.
Sleep disturbance from itching: she was awake till past one scratching.
The rash was described by the family member as hives all over in the disputed childhood penicillin story.
Doctor explicitly said they would not mark the patient as penicillin-allergic based only on the disputed history.
Patient previously tolerated penicillin for tonsillitis in high school without reaction.
Patch testing was explained as only for substances touching the skin, not for food or the antibiotic; those would be judged from the history and response after stopping them.

The doctor advised not to take any more amoxicillin and to start cetirizine that night; the patient repeated understanding to stop the tablets and cream, take cetirizine tonight, and return if not better in two weeks.
